_comment: Cell-identity allowlist for the GSM detector's LAC/ARFCN check (the
2G analogue of signal #5's NGAP NG Setup Request allowlist - see
docs/DETECTION-SIGNALS.md signal #5 and gsm_detector.py's own
docstring for why this same idea applies to 2G).
GSM has no NGAP-style 'setup request' carrying a self-declared cell
identity checked against a database before the network trusts it -
instead the MS learns the serving cell's PLMN/LAC/ARFCN from System
Information broadcasts (BCCH) and presents that same LAI back to the
network in every Location Updating Request. This allowlist lets the
detector flag any LAI (PLMN+LAC) or ARFCN seen on the Um interface
that isn't one of this lab's own known-good cells - useful the same
way signal #5 is: this lab owns ground truth about which cells are
legitimate, so any other LAI/ARFCN appearing is a candidate rogue or
misconfigured cell.
Values below come straight from config/osmocom/osmo-bsc-a5*.cfg (this
lab's one legitimate BTS) - not hardcoded into the detector script,
so the same script works unmodified against a different lab: just
edit this file.
How to read a cell's own identity to add it here:
- plmn.mcc / plmn.mnc: from osmo-bsc-a5*.cfg's 'network country
code' / 'mobile network code', or read directly off a capture
with tshark fields e212.lai.mcc / e212.lai.mnc.
- lac: from osmo-bsc-a5*.cfg's 'bts 0 location_area_code', or read
off a capture with tshark field gsm_a.lac (reported in decimal
here even though the config file writes it in hex, 0x0001 = 1).
- arfcn: from osmo-bsc-a5*.cfg's 'trx 0 arfcn', or tshark field
gsmtap.arfcn.
